title: Memory isolation scheduler and adaptive GPU headroom advisor for inference
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a lightweight scheduler that enforces memory isolation slices for weights / KV / activations and computes an adaptive headroom multiplier per-GPU and per-tenant to reduce OOMs and unnecessary weight offloads while preserving batching efficiency. The advisor must reason about steady-state KV footprint (prefix-heavy workloads), activation variance (burst tokens per request), and weight residency requirements for hot models. Deliver a conservative default policy and an opt-in experimental policy that uses online variance sensors and predictive tail estimates.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can reserve and enforce three memory pools (weights, kv, activations) per GPU with configurable soft/hard bounds.
Adaptive headroom advisor provides per-GPU multiplier (1.0-1.5) computed from last-N minute variance and tail-index; multiplier applied to activations+kv allocations.
Demonstrated reduction in soft-evictions and weight-offloads by >=35% on multi-tenant benchmark (mixed chat + generation) compared to baseline, without increasing 95p latency by >10%.
Rollout plan and canary: feature behind runtime flag with telemetry and automatic rollback if OOM rate increases or P99 latency regresses >15%.
Unit and e2e tests for allocation accounting, and a dashboard with headroom metric, eviction rate, and per-tenant memory breakdown.
notes: 2026-02-10: Kickoff — scoped a lightweight in-runtime advisor and a scheduler shim that can run in host agent. Initial design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/MemIso-Scheduler-Design

2026-02-12: Prototype sensor implemented to compute rolling mean and CV (coefficient of variation) for per-tenant KV and activation footprints. Early results show KV is 60-70% stable for conversational workloads, activations show heavy 95p spikes for summarization requests.

2026-02-14: Decision: use soft reservations for weights (non-evictable), and allow controlled KV spill to NVMe when activations exceed soft headroom. Trade-off: NVMe spill increases token latency for rare bursts but prevents costly weight-offloads which are larger and affect many requests.

2026-02-16: Experimental policy: headroom multiplier = max(1.0, 1 + alpha * CV + beta * tail_index), with alpha/beta tunable per-cluster. Chose alpha=0.35, beta=0.15 after quick tuning on dev cluster. See notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-notebooks/pull/42

2026-02-17: Integration PR opened for scheduler shim + telemetry: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298 — includes memory accounting hooks, per-tenant slice API, and a metrics exporter for headroom_multiplier and kv_spill_count.

2026-02-18: Load test on multi-tenant staging (16 tenants, mixture of chat/generation/rerank). Observed 38% fewer weight-offloads vs baseline, KV-spill events at 0.6% of requests. P99 latency increased 6% for peak bursts — within target. Preparing canary rollout and runbook.
Follow-ups: add a conservatism knob for enterprise clusters, expose recommended multiplier in Console Optimize, and write a migration guide for Dedicated customers with custom quantized weights.
